## Theorem generated by the sources

For the canonical boundary packet `(1/2, -1/2)`, the all-depth
two-boundary balanced Cauchy Gram is independent of the finite source aperture
`M`: it is identically zero for every `M` and every depth. Consequently the
aperture-to-balanced-Gram reporter is noninjective.

The raw bivariate von Mangoldt--Gamma moment row retains exactly the boundary
datum erased by balancing: diagonal Hankel shift invariance holds iff `M = 0`.
Thus every nonempty aperture collides with the empty aperture under the
balanced reporter while remaining separated by the raw Toeplitz--Hankel
reporter.

## Scope and non-patching check

- Both reporters are indexed by the same source aperture `M`.
- The same empty/nonempty pair is used for Gram collision and raw separation.
- Universal two-boundary collapse supplies the full kernel, not a selected
  numerical example.
- Raw shift invariance classifies exactly the quotient information lost.
- No unrelated observable or disjoint case split is appended.

## Novelty status

Post-proof searches covered projected Gram information loss, moment/Hankel
source reconstruction, boundary-mode projection, and Toeplitz--Hankel moment
problems.

Closest sources discuss general orthogonal projection of moment/Gram data and
truncated Toeplitz--Hankel moment reconstruction, but no source found states the
exact finite von Mangoldt--Gamma theorem formalized here: the canonical
`(1/2,-1/2)` balanced Gram is constant over every aperture and every depth,
while every nonempty aperture is separated from the empty one by inequality of
the raw bivariate moment rows, certified by diagonal Hankel shift invariance.

Novelty claim remains narrow: this exact reporter-kernel/raw-separation law,
not orthogonal projection, Gram noninjectivity, or Toeplitz--Hankel
polarization separately.
